newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. agency says more Angolans flee fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency says more Angolans flee fighting.

text.p: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) said on Friday the number of people fleeing fighting in Angola's diamond areas in the northeast had risen to over 5,000.
"The number in Nzage had grown from 3,174 on 17 June to 5,191 by 24 June," the WFP said in a statement after an assessment mission to the area this week.
Nzage is a government-held town in the northeastern-most corner of the Lunda Norte province, near the border of the new Democratic Republic of the Congo.

People deserted remote villagers around Nzage and fled to the town after fighting began in May between the Angolan government and former rebel UNITA over control of diamond-rich areas in the northeast.
The WFP said its officials had found 400 displaced people in the former UNITA-held town of Maludi, south of Nzage, and reported severe cases of malnourished children.
"Of the (displaced), 65 children aged six months to five years were surveyed for malnutrition. Of this group 13.8 percent suffered from severe acute malnutrition," the WFP statement said.
